title: Client-state manipulation and server-side authorization bypass: detect privilege escalation via parameter/cookie tampering
goal: Gruyere's client-state manipulation is a real-world scenario where: the UI restricts admin actions via templates, but the server performs NO authorization check. Attackers manipulate request parameters to gain admin access. This is distinct from IDOR (backlog-223) — it's about parameter/cookie-based privilege escalation. Implement a client-state runner: (1) Hidden field manipulation: identify forms with hidden fields containing role/privilege/user_id values. Modify them and resubmit. If the server accepts the tampered value → finding. (2) Cookie value manipulation: identify cookies containing privilege indicators (role=user, isAdmin=0, access_level=1). Modify values and replay. If accepted → finding 'Cookie-Based Privilege Escalation'. (3) Request parameter privilege manipulation: look for POST/PUT body parameters like role, userType, accountType, isAdmin. Change values and check response. (4) Price/amount manipulation: for any order/payment flows, modify price/quantity values in requests. If server accepts → 'Business Logic: Price Manipulation'. (5) Step-skipping: in multi-step workflows (checkout, admin approval), skip steps by directly requesting step 3 URL without completing steps 1-2. (6) Gruyere-specific: the /newsnippet admin endpoint accessible when admin=True cookie set. Test for similar patterns. Active tier with configured credentials.
scope: Gruyere client-state manipulation (confirmed gap ❌) + WebGoat bypassrestrictions and htmltampering modules. This is one of the most common real-world findings — developers forget server-side validation.
generation_reason: Gruyere's client-state manipulation and WebGoat's bypassrestrictions/htmltampering modules show a gap in server-side authorization testing — parameter/cookie privilege escalation not detected.
